original_value:
Receiving and reacting to notifications on mobile devices can be cumbersome. We propose MuscleIO, the use of electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) for notification output and electromyography (EMG) for reacting to notifications. Our approach provides a one-handed, eyes-free, and low-effort way of dealing with notifications. We built a prototype that interleaves muscle input and muscle output signals using the same electrodes. EMS and EMG alternate such that the EMG input signal is measured in the gaps of the EMS output signal, so voluntary muscle contraction is measured during muscle stimulation.
          Notifications are represented as EMS signals and are accepted or refused either by a directional or a time-based EMG response. A lab user study with 12 participants shows that the directional EMG response is superior to the time-based response in terms of reaction time, error rate, and user preference. Furthermore, the directional approach is the fastest and the most intuitive for users compared to a button-based smartwatch interface as a baseline.

result.paraphrase: Receiving and responding to notifications on mobile devices can be cumbersome. We propose MuscleIO, which uses electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) to deliver notifications and electromyography (EMG) to react to them. The approach offers a one-handed, eyes-free, low-effort way to handle notifications. We built a prototype that alternates muscle input and muscle output signals on the same electrodes. EMS and EMG are interleaved so that the EMG input signal is measured in the gaps between EMS output signals, allowing voluntary muscle contraction to be measured during muscle stimulation. Notifications are encoded as EMS signals and can be accepted or rejected via either a directional or time-based EMG response. A lab user study with 12 participants showed that the directional EMG response outperforms the time-based response in reaction time, error rate, and user preference. In addition, the directional method is the fastest and most intuitive for users compared with a button-based smartwatch interface used as a baseline.
